task:
This is a mechanism check. Do not produce a plan and do not write files.

Inspect the project workspace's recorded journal entries. For each entry, report its kind, its
title, and one sentence on what it establishes. Then state which entry (or entries) bear on the
question "should the trust run Friday evening events in 2026?" and why. If an entry is stale or
misleading, say so and say what in the source pack contradicts it.

| 3 | `REFERENCE_NOTE` | East hall is climate-controlled | That the 2019 building survey described the east hall as climate-controlled and fit for sensitive textiles and paper. |
| 4 | `REFERENCE_NOTE` | Members want evening events | That 61% of survey respondents named transport as the main barrier and 44% said they would attend an evening event if transport were available. |
| 5 | `REFERENCE_NOTE` | Website migration | That the site moved domain in March 2024 and traffic rose 12%. |

## Entries bearing on "should the trust run Friday evening events in 2026?"

**Entry 1 (2023 pilot) — directly and decisively.** It is the only local behavioural evidence about Friday evenings: real attendance, not stated preference. But it is also the entry that most needs re-reading (see below), because its own conclusion — "unless transport is in place" — is the operative condition, and the pack shows transport was tried and defunded rather than never arranged.

**Entry 4 (Members want evening events) — directly, but only as weak evidence.** It is the only forward-looking demand signal, yet it is a hypothetical: the survey's own method note says respondents were "asked to imagine a bus", that willingness to attend was not tested and willingness to pay was not asked. Only 44% said yes (about 106 of 610 members), 35% said no, and on the separate time-preference question weekday evening was the *least* popular usable slot at 18% against 38% for Saturday morning. It supports *testing* an evening offer, not committing to a series.

**Entry 2 (Saturday childcare) — indirectly, as opportunity cost.** It is the one intervention in the pack that moved attendance, it runs in the same staff pool (evening events need two staff present), and the family fund behind it is capped at £9,000 and uncommitted. It bears on whether Friday evenings are the best use of scarce staff attention and of the £60,000, not on whether evenings would work.

**Entry 3 (East hall) — indirectly, as a scheduling constraint.** If Friday events are planned in the east hall (120 seated, the natural film room), they cannot run there in January–February 2026; the west hall seats 60 and the workshop room has no blackout. It bears on *when and where*, not *whether*.

**Entry 5 (Website migration) — not decision-bearing.** At most a note on the marketing channel; the pack explicitly says there is no evidence it changed attendance.

## Stale or misleading entries, and what contradicts them

**Entry 3 is stale and should not be relied on.** Its own provenance says "2019 building survey, carried forward". `staff-interviews.md` (PB, building officer) states flatly: "The east hall was recorded as climate-controlled in the 2019 survey. That is no longer true. The HVAC unit failed in January 2025." `spaces-and-costs.md` and `constraints.md` agree: the hall is unavailable for activities needing stable temperature or humidity until the repair is complete and commissioned, with completion only *expected* late February 2026 and dependent on a capital grant not yet approved. `open-questions.md` question 3 flags exactly this risk for a textile exhibition. Anyone reading entry 3 as current would plan a sensitive-material show into an unconditioned room.

**Entry 1 is misleading in its causal claim and its framing.** It says "the pilot had no transport arrangement". `staff-interviews.md` (RS, volunteer driver) contradicts that: "We trialled a minibus for three nights in 2023. It stopped when the funding for the driver ran out." So there *was* a transport arrangement; it was withdrawn. `prior-interventions.md` reinforces that the content was not the problem — the programmer's note reads "people liked the films; the problem was getting home" — and booking data shows 60 seats reserved for the first night and 48 for the second, so the 37/23/19 slide tracks transport failure, not lack of interest. Calling it a failed pilot, and implying transport was never tried, invites the wrong conclusion (drop evenings) when the pack supports the narrower one (fund evenings only with a funded way home). Note also that the recorded recommendation itself already carries that condition — it is the title and the "no transport arrangement" clause that mislead.

**Entry 4 is misleading by inference.** "This supports an evening series" overstates what the survey can bear: the volunteer's method note disclaims the very figure being used, and the 61% transport figure is about attendance in general, not about evenings. Read together with entry 1, the honest reading is that transport is the binding constraint in both directions — which makes a *funded* Friday trial a coherent test, and an unfunded one a repeat of 2023.

**Entry 2 is imprecise rather than wrong.** `attendance-2024-2025.csv` gives 26.9 for January–August 2024, but 40.0 for September–December 2024, not 42. The "42" is the October–December average (41, 44, 42) — the months when childcare was fully running, one of which was a Christmas special. The direction of the claim survives; the number in the entry does not, and September (33, "childcare pilot begins") is a transition month that dilutes the four-month window.

**Entry 5 is accurate but incomplete in a way that matters little here.** It omits the pack's own caveat that traffic growth did not translate into attendance and the decline continued through 2025.","toolCalls":["tool/call:palimpsest_project","tool/result","tool/call:bash","tool/result","tool/call:bash","tool/result","tool/call:read","tool/call:read","tool/call:read","tool/call:read","tool/call:read","tool/call:read","tool/call:read","tool/call:read","tool/result","tool/result","tool/result","tool/result","tool/result","tool/result","tool/result","tool/result","tool/call:bash","tool/result"]}

entries.title: 2023 evening pilot failed
entries.body: Three Friday evening screenings in October-December 2023 drew 37, 23 and 19 people. The last scheduled minibus leaves the square at 18:40 and the pilot had no transport arrangement. Do not fund Friday evening opening again unless transport is in place.

entries.title: Saturday childcare raised attendance
entries.body: From September 2024, free childcare alongside the Saturday family workshop raised average attendance from 27 in the first eight months of 2024 to 42 in the last four. The family fund paid 180 pounds per session.

entries.title: East hall is climate-controlled
entries.body: The 2019 building survey recorded the east hall as climate-controlled and suitable for sensitive textiles and paper.

entries.title: Members want evening events
entries.body: 61 percent of members say transport is the main barrier and 44 percent say they would attend an evening event if transport were available. This supports an evening series.

entries.title: Website migration
entries.body: The website moved to a new domain in March 2024 and traffic rose 12 percent.
